speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you've been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any fever or changes in your bowel or urinary habits?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of tuberculosis, HIV, or recent travel to areas where these are common? Also, can you describe the specific location of your abdominal pain and whether you've noticed any lumps or swelling elsewhere on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Doctor: The fact that the swollen node feels fixed is concerning, so have you experienced any recent cough, shortness of breath, or changes in your appetite? Also, do you have any family history of cancer or autoimmune disorders?

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_CT_Scan
Given your fixed node and abdominal fullness, I need to check for internal organ involvement immediately. Do you have any history of alcohol use or chronic liver conditions?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal CT Scan findings indicate slight abdominal distension with dullness noted over the left lower quadrant. Splenomegaly is detected. Additionally, the CT scan of the thorax and abdomen reveals massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT confirms massive lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly, so do you experience any itching or a burning sensation in your lymph nodes after drinking alcohol? Given these findings, I will now proceed to order a lymph node biopsy. REQUEST TEST: Lymph_Node_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Biopsy of the cervical lymph node reveals lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20. Additionally, blood work shows elevated White Blood Cell (WBC) count, slightly decreased Hemoglobin, and elevated Lactate Dehydrogenase (LDH) levels. Vital signs remain stable with a temperature of 36.8°C, blood pressure of 135/80 mmHg, heart rate of 82 bpm, and respiratory rate of 14 breaths/min.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy showing CD20-positive lymphocytes with a high proliferative index, combined with your B-symptoms and massive lymphadenopathy, strongly points to a specific type of aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma. DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL)
